strengths: The paper addresses an important multimodal inference bottleneck with a simple combination of class-attention pruning and similarity-based token merging. Reducing tokens before the LLM is practically relevant and requires no learned compression module.
PruMerge+ demonstrates a useful accuracy–compression tradeoff. With reportedly 25% of visual tokens, the 7B model achieves 76.8 versus 78.5 on VQAv2 and 64.9 versus 64.3 on MMBench (Table 1).

Evaluation covers six image benchmarks, two LLM sizes, and three video benchmarks. Inference-only transfer to Video-LLaVA is particularly encouraging: PruMerge largely preserves performance and improves ActivityNet-QA accuracy from 45.3 to 48.3 (Table 3).

The ablations provide evidence for token supplementation and fine-tuning. Adding supplementation improves MME from 1221.6 to 1350.3 (Table 5), and Table 6 explicitly distinguishes training-free and fine-tuned results. Source models, datasets, and component methods are cited.
weaknesses: The central deployment-efficiency claim lacks measured validation. Table 2 reports roofline estimates for LLM prefill, rather than actual latency, throughput, or peak memory. End-to-end measurements including vision encoding, selection/merging overhead, and decoding are needed, particularly for PruMerge+, which provides the stronger accuracy results.

Comparisons do not adequately establish the advantage of the proposed adaptive strategy. Table 4 compares against sequential and uniform sampling, but lacks fixed-budget attention top-k selection and established token-merging baselines such as the cited ToMe. Matched token budgets and fine-tuning conditions would help isolate the contributions of adaptivity and merging from simply retaining more tokens.

Important implementation details are ambiguous. Algorithm 1 adds m uniformly sampled tokens to m selected tokens, which would turn 5.5% retention into approximately 11%, rather than the reported 25% for PruMerge+. The neighbor count k is unspecified, and the merging update excludes the selected center and lacks normalization despite descriptions of weighted averaging. Attention-head aggregation and LoRA hyperparameters are also missing. These issues prevent confident reproduction of the reported operating points.

The repeated claims of preserving performance substantially overstate the aggressive variant's results. For the 7B model, PruMerge reduces VQAv2 from 78.5 to 72.0, POPE from 85.9 to 76.3, and MME from 1510.7 to 1350.3 (Table 1). These may be worthwhile efficiency tradeoffs, but they are not merely negligible losses. Section 4.1 also incorrectly claims improved POPE performance. The contribution should be framed around the demonstrated tradeoff, with stronger efficiency and comparative evidence to support acceptance.
